summary: Isaac Asimov was a male science fiction writer, novelist, and university teacher born in Petrovichi, Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic. He was married to Janet Asimov and worked as a biochemist, journalist, and science writer. Asimov received numerous awards, including the Hugo Award, Nebula Award, and Locus Award, and was also a Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and the Committee for Skeptical Inquiry. He studied at various institutions, including Boys High School, Columbia University School of General Science, and Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science.

Arthur C. Clarke was a male physicist, inventor, futurist, novelist, non-fiction writer, science fiction writer, and explorer. He attended King's College London and Richard Huish College, Taunton. Clarke was a member of the Royal Air Force and held agnostic beliefs. He received numerous awards, including the Hugo Award, Nebula Award, and Knight Bachelor, and was buried at Kanatte Cemetery.

Robert A. Heinlein was a male American author who wrote in the genres of fantasy, hard science fiction, military science fiction, and young adult literature. He attended the United States Naval Academy and was a naval officer. Heinlein won numerous awards, including the Hugo Award for Best Novel, Locus Award for Best Novel, and Damon Knight Memorial Grand Master Award. He died of heart failure in Carmel-by-the-Sea, with some of his notable works being Starship Troopers, Stranger in a Strange Land, and Have Space Suit—Will Travel.

Ray Bradbury was an American author influenced by writers such as Aldous Huxley, Edgar Rice Burroughs, and H. P. Lovecraft. He wrote in multiple genres, including fantasy, horror literature, and social science fiction, and is known for works like Fahrenheit 451, The Martian Chronicles, and Something Wicked This Way Comes. Bradbury was born in Waukegan and died in Los Angeles, and was buried in Westwood Village Memorial Park Cemetery. He was a recipient of numerous awards, including the National Medal of Arts, the Damon Knight Memorial Grand Master Award, and the Pulitzer Prize Special Citations and Awards.

Frank Herbert was a male American novelist, journalist, and science fiction writer. He was born in Tacoma and attended the University of Washington, Lincoln High School, and North Salem High School. Herbert won several awards, including the Hugo Award for Best Novel, Nebula Award for Best Novel, and Seiun Award for Best Translated Long Work. He was married to Flora Lillian Parkinson and Theresa Diane Shackelford, and his son Brian Herbert is also a writer.

Philip K. Dick was a male novelist, philosopher, essayist, and science fiction writer. He attended the University of California, Berkeley, and Berkeley High School. Dick is known for his works such as Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, Ubik, The Man in the High Castle, and the VALIS trilogy, and has won awards including the Hugo Award for Best Novel and the John W. Campbell Memorial Award for Best Science Fiction Novel. He was married to multiple women, including Anne R. Dick, Nancy Hackett, and Tessa B. Dick, and had children, including Isa Dick Hackett, Laura Leslie, and Christopher Dick.

Ursula K. Le Guin was an author, translator, journalist, literary critic, and children's writer from Berkeley. She wrote in the genres of fantasy and feminist science fiction, and was recognized with numerous awards, including the Hugo Award, Nebula Award, and National Book Award. Le Guin attended the University of Oregon and Berkeley High School, and was the daughter of Alfred L. Kroeber and Theodora Kroeber. She received a Fulbright Scholarship and won various other awards, such as the Locus Award, World Fantasy Award, and PEN/Malamud Award.

George Orwell was a human who was born in Motihari and died in London. He was educated at institutions including Wellington College, Eton College, and University College London. Orwell was involved in various activities, including serving in the International Brigades and the British Broadcasting Corporation, and was affiliated with organizations such as the Independent Labour Party and the Workers' Party of Marxist Unification. He was also a recipient of awards like the Hugo Award for Best Novella and the Prometheus Award - Hall of Fame.

Douglas Adams was a male novelist, playwright, comedian, musician, children's writer, and science fiction writer. He was born in Cambridge and died in Santa Barbara. Adams was a member of the Footlights and Groucho Club, and attended Brentwood School and St John's College. He received awards including the Locus Award for Best Science Fiction Novel, Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation, and Inkpot Award.

H. G. Wells was a male author from the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, born in Bromley. He was influenced by Thomas Henry Huxley and wrote several notable works, including The War of the Worlds, The Time Machine, and The Invisible Man. Wells was also the president of an organization and had children, including Anthony West, George Philip Wells, and Frank Wells. He died of natural causes and was featured in various encyclopedias, such as Encyclopædia Britannica and the Great Soviet Encyclopedia.
